title: Loop phase output and head advance
statement: Let $c,C,q$ be natural numbers with $q>0$, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $i<c+1$. Suppose $h\colon\{0,\ldots,c\}\to\mathbb Z$ satisfies $h(k)=0$ whenever $k\le i$. For natural numbers $r,j$ with $j+r=q$ and any Boolean output word $o$, start in state $\mathrm{loop}(i)$ with tape-head positions obtained from $h$ by setting position $i$ to $j$. After $r(\mathrm{cost}(q,C,i)+2)+q+2$ steps, the machine is in state $\mathrm{advance}(i+1)$ with head positions $h$ and output $o$ followed by $rCq^i$ copies of true.
